summary: Well‑executed, fully preregistered paired study comparing an LLM-alone observation to a deterministic verifier+gate (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Execution artifacts are comprehensive and consistent with the preregistration; the confirmatory result is a degenerate null (all 200 shared initial candidates were valid). The manuscript correctly documents design, limitations, and provenance, but needs a small, evidence-resolvable bibliographic clarification before finalisation.
required_revisions: Provide a conventional IEEE‑style numbered References section (authors, title, venue, year, DOI/URL as supplementary) in the manuscript PDF: do not leave the References as bare DOI/arXiv/identifier strings. Ensure each numbered reference's metadata in the bibliography matches the archived verified records and that the in‑text numeric citations map correctly to those bibliography entries.

Confirm in a single concise sentence placed in Methods (and repeated in the Disclosure if desired) that the preregistered and executed generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate (one initial sampled generation reused by both arms per pair), that therefore the confirmatory estimand measures only validator/repair/gate effects on identical first‑pass candidates (not guarded‑conditioned regeneration or multi‑sample model variance), and that this design choice explains the degenerate contingency (n11=200) and the resulting zero-width bootstrap CI. (This clarification must be supported by the archived execution artifacts already supplied and need not require new experiments.)
optional_revisions: Add a one-row summary table (or brief sentence) giving counts of task difficulty labels (e.g., how many 'very_hard' vs 'extreme') from the archived task_manifest.jsonl to help readers assess task-bank hardness.

Mention explicitly in Discussion why the paired bootstrap produced a zero-width 95% CI in the observed degenerate case (brief justification that no discordant pairs produce no observable paired variation under the shared_initial_candidate design).

Discuss, briefly, how an alternative confirmatory design (independent per‑condition generation or multiple samples per condition) would change the primary estimand and the model‑call accounting, so readers can directly map this run's null result to follow‑up designs.
